strongest_angle: Explore how rummy-nose tetra fish navigate groups in a November 2026 virtual reality experiment by focusing on a single influential neighbor instead of all four surrounding entities.

key_facts.fact: Guy Theraulaz and his colleagues at the National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS) and the University of Toulouse in France built a virtual-reality environment to study how schooling fish coordinate their behavior.

During the virtual reality experiments published around October and November 2026, a rummy-nose tetra fish swam freely in a bowl while real-time images of virtual fish were projected onto the walls around it.
The research team programmed four virtual fish with different rules of interaction and ran eight one-hour trials for each setup to test how the rummy-nose tetra responds to influential neighbors.
